learn.title: Iron-Air Batteries: Long-Duration Storage
learn.intro: Iron-air batteries store energy for 100+ hours using iron and air, offering a low-cost, scalable solution for balancing renewable grids. Unlike short-term storage, they can power cities during prolonged solar/wind gaps, making them vital for 24/7 clean energy. Their simplicity and abundance of materials make them a game-changer for energy security.
learn.c1_text: Iron-air batteries store energy by reacting iron with oxygen. When charged, iron oxidizes; during discharge, it reforms. This process is reversible and uses abundant materials. For example, a 100 kWh battery could power a home for days, ideal for renewable energy backup.
learn.c2_text: They’re cheaper and safer than lithium-ion batteries. Lithium costs $100/kWh vs. iron’s $20/kWh. They also don’t degrade as fast, lasting 20+ years. A 2023 study showed a 500 kWh iron-air system could store energy from a 1 MW solar farm for 24 hours.
learn.c3_text: India could deploy iron-air batteries in solar farms to manage grid fluctuations. With 140 GW solar target by 2030, these batteries could reduce reliance on coal. A 2024 pilot in Rajasthan stored 50 MWh for 12 hours, cutting diesel use by 40% during peak demand.
learn.stat1: India plans 10 GW iron-air storage by 2030 (CEA, 2024)
learn.stat2: Iron costs 1/5th of lithium per kWh (BloombergNEF, 2023)
learn.stat3: A 1 MW iron-air system stores 500 kWh (NREL, 2023)

learn.title: Agrivoltaics: Farming + Solar Panels
learn.intro: Agrivoltaics combines solar panels with farming, using land for both energy and crops. This dual-use approach boosts yields, reduces water use, and creates jobs. It’s a sustainable solution for rural areas, turning unused land into clean energy hubs.
learn.c1_text: Solar panels are installed above crops, allowing sunlight to reach plants. For example, in the Netherlands, strawberries grow under panels, increasing yield by 15%. The system uses tracking to adjust sun exposure, balancing energy and agriculture.
learn.c2_text: Farmers earn dual income from crops and energy sales. A 2022 NREL study showed a 30% increase in income for farms using agrivoltaics. Panels also reduce evaporation, saving water—critical in drought-prone regions like Rajasthan.
learn.c3_text: India’s agrivoltaics projects are rising, with 50 MW installed by 2024. The government supports this via subsidies. A Gujarat pilot combined solar with wheat farming, boosting crop output by 20% while generating 2 MW of power.
learn.stat1: India aims for 5 GW agrivoltaics by 2028 (MNRE, 2024)
learn.stat3: 50 MW agrivoltaics installed in India (2024 data)
learn.stat4: Global agrivoltaics market to hit $1B by 2030 (IRENA, 2024)

learn.title: Hydrogen Colors: Blue, Green, Grey
learn.intro: Hydrogen’s ‘color’ reflects its production method. Green hydrogen uses renewable energy, blue uses fossil fuels with carbon capture, and grey emits CO2. Understanding these distinctions is key to decarbonizing industries like shipping and steel. Choosing the right color impacts climate goals.
learn.c1_text: Grey hydrogen comes from natural gas without capture (90% of global production). Blue adds carbon capture, reducing emissions by 70%. Green uses renewable electricity to split water, emitting zero CO2. For example, a 100 MW green electrolyzer needs 150 MWh of solar power daily.
learn.c2_text: Grey hydrogen emits 10 kg CO2 per kg H2, while green emits none. Blue cuts emissions to 2-3 kg CO2/kg H2. A 2023 IEA report showed blue hydrogen could reduce shipping emissions by 40% if scaled by 2030, but green is preferable for net-zero goals.
learn.c3_text: India aims for 5 GW green hydrogen by 2030. The National Hydrogen Mission supports blue hydrogen for industries. A 2024 pilot in Odisha produced 100 kg/day green hydrogen using solar, cutting local emissions by 500 tons annually.
learn.stat1: India’s green hydrogen target: 5 GW by 2030 (NHM, 2024)
learn.stat2: Grey hydrogen emits 10 kg CO2/kg H2 (IEA, 2023)

learn.title: Green Ammonia: Clean Fuel & Fertilizer
learn.intro: Green ammonia is produced using renewable energy, offering a zero-emission alternative to fossil fuels. It powers ships and replaces synthetic fertilizers, reducing agriculture’s carbon footprint. With global demand for ammonia at 200 million tons/year, green ammonia could revolutionize energy and farming.
learn.c1_text: Green ammonia combines green hydrogen with nitrogen from the air. A 1 MW electrolyzer produces 100 kg hydrogen daily, which reacts with nitrogen to form ammonia. This process requires 2-3 GJ of renewable energy per ton of ammonia, making it sustainable.
learn.c2_text: Ammonia burns cleanly, emitting only water vapor. A 2023 ship trial in Singapore used 500 tons of green ammonia, cutting CO2 by 1,000 tons. It’s safer than methanol and easier to store than hydrogen, making it ideal for heavy transport.
learn.c3_text: India produces 25 million tons of ammonia annually for fertilizers. Replacing 30% with green ammonia could cut emissions by 15 million tons yearly. The government plans to incentivize green ammonia plants near coal mines, using waste CO2 for synthesis.
learn.stat2: Green ammonia reduces fertilizer emissions by 40% (IRENA, 2024)
learn.stat3: 1,000 tons of green ammonia used in shipping (Singapore, 2023)
learn.stat4: Global green ammonia market to hit $5B by 2030 (BloombergNEF, 2024)

learn.title: Solar Inverters: String vs Micro vs Hybrid
learn.intro: Solar inverters convert DC solar panel output to AC power. String inverters handle multiple panels, micro inverters work per panel, and hybrid inverters manage batteries. Choosing the right type affects efficiency, cost, and grid resilience. Understanding these options helps optimize solar systems for homes and businesses.
learn.c1_text: String inverters connect multiple panels in a ‘string.’ If one panel fails, the whole string loses power. They’re cheaper ($0.10/W) and simpler. For example, a 5 kW system with 20 panels uses one string inverter, ideal for unshaded roofs.
learn.c2_text: Micro inverters attach to each panel, optimizing individual performance. If one panel is shaded, others still work. They cost $0.20/W but increase efficiency by 5-10%. A 5 kW system with micro inverters can generate 6 kWh/day compared to 5.5 kWh with string inverters.
learn.c3_text: Hybrid inverters manage solar and battery storage. They store excess energy for night use. A 5 kW hybrid system with a 10 kWh battery can power a home for 12 hours. India’s 2024 subsidies make hybrid inverters cost-effective for off-grid villages.
learn.stat1: India installed 10 GW hybrid inverters in 2024 (CEA, 2024)

learn.title: Carbon Markets: Clean Energy Incentives
learn.intro: Carbon markets allow companies to buy/sell emission permits. Credits incentivize clean energy by penalizing polluters. For example, a factory reducing emissions can sell credits to others. This system drives investment in renewables, making it a key tool for global climate action.
learn.c1_text: Companies emit CO2 and must offset it via credits. One credit equals 1 ton of CO2 reduced. A solar farm generating 1 MW saves 1,500 tons/year, earning credits to sell. A 2023 report showed 100 million credits traded globally, worth $50B.
learn.c2_text: Credits come from projects like wind farms or reforestation. Verified Emission Reductions (VERs) are traded on exchanges. A 2024 IEA study found that 1 credit in India costs $5-$10, making it affordable for small businesses to participate.
learn.c3_text: India’s carbon credit market launched in 2023, targeting 2 billion credits by 2030. A Tamil Nadu solar farm earned 500,000 credits in 2024, selling them to meet compliance. The government plans to link credits to renewable subsidies.
learn.stat1: India’s carbon credit market: 2B credits target by 2030 (IEA, 2024)
